A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D Field of Junctions work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original CT reconstruction experiments, cryo-ET denoising examples, point-cloud evaluations, and hyperparameter ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds quantitative cryo-ET evaluation, NAF comparisons, curved-tube experiments, resource measurements, and an empirical convergence analysis.

M1.justification: The junction parameterization, objective, smooth indicators, initialization/refinement procedure, and approximate proximal updates are unchanged. The eight-region configuration used in the new curved-tube study was already defined and evaluated in v1; it is not a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five CT volumes, four cryo-ET datasets, and 28 PointCleanNet shapes. v2 adds a synthetic 64^3 curved-tube denoising scenario to examine curved geometry under different local patch supports (Section 10.5).

E2.justification: v2 adds Neural Attenuation Fields (NAF) to the reported CT comparisons in Tables 1 and 4 and the corresponding figures. The reported cryo-ET and point-cloud comparator sets are retained; the additional mention of 3D TV in point-cloud preprocessing is not accompanied by comparison results.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 introduces a substantial quantitative evaluation protocol for previously qualitative-only cryo-ET results: even/odd projection splitting, independent reconstruction and denoising, and corrected FSC with resolution thresholds of 0.5 and 0.25. The new curved-tube experiment sweeps patch sizes 4–12 and compares M=3 with M=8. Existing CT and point-cloud evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained engine ablations, v2 directly tests curvature preservation versus patch size and region count, measures the associated runtime/memory tradeoff, and plots update norms for approximate proximal reconstruction (Sections 10.5–10.6, Figures 15–16). These add substantive evidence about geometric limitations and optimization behavior.

E5.justification: Section 10.3 newly specifies fixed-seed within-voxel jitter, without giving the seed value or establishing a change in runs. Table 2 retains mean±standard deviation across shapes; neither version adds repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing CT, point-cloud, and engine-ablation scores are unchanged, but v2 adds NAF scores, FSC results, resource measurements, and curved-tube/convergence findings. Figure 5 reports 32.14 Å for 3D FoJ versus 39.86 Å for SC-Net at corrected FSC=0.25; at 0.5, SC-Net is better, 55.60 versus 58.24 Å. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical model and optimization equations are retained. The 2D objective moves from the main text to appendix Section 7. The added FSC correction is an adopted evaluation formula, and the convergence plot supplies empirical observations rather than a theorem, proof, or new derivation.

C1.justification: The central training-free geometric-prior and inverse-problem contributions remain. v2 qualifies superiority claims to the evaluated classical, untrained-neural, and noisy-example-trained methods, and replaces the contribution bullets' broad outperforming statement with strong performance across the three applications.

C2.justification: v2 corrects v1's claims of consistently winning CT metrics: Sections 5.1 and 10.1 acknowledge mixed PSNR rankings and distinguish structural fidelity from PSNR. It also adds a substantive piecewise-planar limitation, explaining curvature-dependent failure conditions and the expressivity/resource tradeoff of using eight regions, supported by the new curved-tube study.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: ground-truth-anchored voxel grids, 10-voxel padding, nearest-center assignment, jitter, cryo-ET dimensions, hyperparameter guidance, and task-specific runtime/peak-memory measurements. These are disclosures, not demonstrated changes to existing experiments. The abstract adds a repository link and says code is available, although the introduction still promises release upon publication; actual availability remains unresolved from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Harauz–van Heel reference supporting FSC and the NAF paper. It more explicitly positions explicit geometric modeling as complementary to pretrained generative priors and explains the comparison scope excluding paired-clean-data training. The broader related-work framework is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized rewrites to the introduction, related work, experimental discussion, and limitations; condenses the contribution bullets; and swaps the first two authors' order. It relocates the 2D objective explanation to the appendix and adds analysis subsections while retaining the overall narrative and method organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds the FSC plot/result table, resource Table 8, curved-tube figure, and convergence plot. It expands CT comparison grids with NAF, restructures Table 4 into side-by-side metric panels with best-value bolding, and enlarges/repositions the centriole display. Existing point-cloud and engine-ablation displays are principally retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses: cryo-ET gains a specified quantitative FSC evaluation instead of relying solely on visual judgments, CT comparisons gain NAF, and curvature limitations receive direct experimental support. It also corrects CT interpretations contradicted by the unchanged tables and discloses consequential preprocessing and resource details. Together these substantially improve evidential support, transparency, and calibration of conclusions. The inconsistent code-release statements and limited scope of the new FSC/convergence tests remain shortcomings but do not outweigh these gains.
